interval_rules: A targeted review set (e.g. the windows olmoearth_review_set lists) is not a sample: its error rate overstates the map's, 1.8 to 5.8 times on the package's exp78.

The simple-random-sample interval p +/- 1.96 sqrt(p(1 - p)/n) does not apply to a stratified or targeted design, nor to a pool of both; report the interval and method olmoearth_estimate_map_error returns instead.
result.report: Report the estimate with [low, high] and the method string as returned; the rate is of the design's population windows.

result.verdict: No zone is certified at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1 under rule 'prefix': no share of the map is shown to be wrong at most alpha=0.05 of the time.

levels_tested.how_the_rule_tests_them: prefix tests the 18 levels at delta = 0.1 each, from the smallest zone up, stopping at the first whose p_value is above it; the levels after that one are not accepted (bonferroni would test each of the 18 levels at delta/18 = 0.1/18 = 0.00555556)
levels_tested.why_these_levels: a zone must hold at least 45 labels to be certified at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1 (min_labels_to_certify), so with 300 labels no zone below coverage c_min = 0.15 is tested; another alpha tests other levels

result.reading_levels: Each level's upper_bound is that zone's own bound at delta, before the rule is applied. A level whose upper_bound is below alpha, this alpha or any other, is not thereby certified: certification is the package's exact test under the chosen rule (levels_tested says how this rule tested which levels), and which levels are tested depends on alpha. Only a level marked accepted at this call's alpha is certified. Another alpha tests other levels, so this output says nothing about it; and the guarantee holds for an alpha fixed before the labels were seen, so trying looser alphas until one certifies is not covered by it.
result.design_requirement: Certification needs design='random' (a simple random sample of the map); olmoearth_certify_zone refuses a 'confidence' or 'proportional' design, so recommend only a random design for a certified zone.

content:
Short answer: none. With these 300 random labels, no share of the map certifies as wrong at most 5% of the time (rule `prefix`, delta = 0.1).

**Overall map error** (from your simple random sample, n = 300 of 15,813 windows):
- Estimate: **23%** wrong, 95% interval **[18.4%, 28.1%]**
- Method: exact hypergeometric interval (simple random sample of a finite map)

**Certification at alpha = 0.05 — every tested zone rejected:**

| Zone (top-confident share) | Labels inside | Wrong inside | Upper bound | Accepted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15% (smallest testable) | 46 | 3 | 13.9% | ✗ |
| 25% | 68 | 3 | 9.5% | ✗ |
| 50% | 140 | 13 | 13.2% | ✗ |
| 100% (whole map) | 300 | 69 | 26.4% | ✗ |

Even the best-15% slice contains 3 wrong windows out of 46 labelled ones, putting its exact upper bound near 13.9% — well above the 5% bar. Stricter rules (bonferroni) would only reject more.

Note the guarantee applies to an alpha fixed *before* seeing the labels, so I did not re-test at looser thresholds. To certify anything, you'd need more random labels concentrated where the map is most confident (currently only 46 labels sit inside the top-15% slice). If you want, I can plan a targeted follow-up random sample focused on the high-confidence regions.
